events.reason: Right upper lobectomy for lung cancer

reports.text:
SPECIMENS: A. Lung, right upper lobe, lobectomy. B-E. Mediastinal and hilar lymph nodes (stations 2R, 4R, 7, 10R, 11R).
GROSS: Right upper lobe, 15.5 x 9.0 x 4.0 cm. A firm tan-white mass, 2.0 cm in greatest dimension, lies 2.5 cm from the bronchial margin and does not pucker the pleura.
MICROSCOPIC: Invasive adenocarcinoma. Visceral pleura not involved. No lymphovascular invasion identified.
MARGINS: Bronchial, vascular and parenchymal margins negative.
LYMPH NODES: 0 of 9 lymph nodes involved.
PATHOLOGIC STAGE: pT1b N0 (AJCC 8th edition), stage IA2.
reports.conclusion: Invasive adenocarcinoma of the right upper lobe, 2.0 cm, margins negative, 0/9 nodes, pT1b N0, stage IA2.

documents.title: Thoracic surgery discharge summary
documents.author: thoracic surgery
documents.body:
Discharge Summary - Thoracic Surgery
Admitted: 01/10/2023  Discharged: 01/13/2023

Procedure 01/10: video-assisted thoracoscopic right upper lobectomy with mediastinal lymph node dissection. Uncomplicated. Single chest tube removed postoperative day 2 after air leak resolved. Stress-dose hydrocortisone given perioperatively and tapered back to his home prednisone by discharge. Tacrolimus continued with levels checked by the transplant team; creatinine stable at baseline.

Final pathology: invasive adenocarcinoma, 2.0 cm, all margins negative, 0 of 9 nodes, pT1b N0, stage IA2.

Condition at discharge: ambulating independently, room air saturations normal, pain controlled.
Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge medications: home medications unchanged (tacrolimus 5 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, albuterol as needed). Naproxen held for now.
Instructions: no lifting over 10 lb or driving for 2 weeks; walking daily. Thoracic surgery clinic in 2-3 weeks; oncology to review pathology. PCP follow-up in 1-2 weeks.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
10 days post VATS RUL lobectomy. Walking 2 miles a day. Some soreness at the port sites and along the right side, settling. The cough he had before surgery is fading. No fever, no sputum, no leg swelling. Appetite back.
Path came back stage IA2 adenocarcinoma, nodes negative - surgeon and oncology going over it with him next month.
Meds: home regimen, has not restarted naproxen.
Exam: afebrile, sat normal on RA. Incisions clean and dry, no erythema. Breath sounds slightly reduced R apex, no crackles. Calves soft.
A/P: recovering well. Pathology reviewed with him. Keep walking. Oncology and surgery f/u scheduled. Return to driving cleared by surgery on their timeline.

documents.title: Thoracic oncology consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Thoracic Oncology
Visit date: 02/15/2023

Dear colleague,
I saw Mr. Moran after his right upper lobectomy for a 2.0 cm adenocarcinoma, pT1b N0, stage IA2, with negative margins. He has recovered well and is back to walking and light jogging.

For completely resected stage IA disease, adjuvant systemic therapy is not recommended, and he agrees. Plan surveillance CT chest every 6 months for 2 years, then yearly. Next scan July 2023.

Allergies: NKDA. Medications: per your list; tacrolimus and prednisone per transplant.

Thank you for involving us.
Thoracic Oncology

documents.title: Thoracic surgery postoperative visit
documents.author: thoracic surgery
documents.body: Postoperative visit 02/01/2023: incisions healed, lungs expanding well on chest film, no air or fluid. Cleared to drive and return to work 2/13. Can resume running gradually. Discharged from surgical follow-up; surveillance with oncology.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Atorvastatin 40 mg refill request from pharmacy. Lipids 5/2022. Sent 90 days x 1; due for labs at May visit.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine f/u. Back to full-time driving since February and running 3 days a week, about 10-12 miles total. Breathing fine. Weight coming back.

He brought a printout about a research trial of a new cholesterol drug that is recruiting people with high LDL and asked if he should sign up. Went through how a study like that runs: people are assigned by chance to the new drug or a dummy pill, they measure LDL over a few months, and a short study can't tell you much about heart attacks or rare side effects. Told him he's welcome to call the study line, though his transplant medicines and recent cancer surgery may keep him out. He's not sure he wants the extra visits with his schedule. Not enrolled.

Meds unchanged. Hasn't gone back to naproxen much since surgery, a few times for the knees.
Exam: BP as charted. Lungs clear, slightly decreased R apex. Heart regular. No edema.
A/P: HTN controlled. Lipids today on atorvastatin 40. Post-lobectomy, surveillance CT in July via oncology. Physical late summer.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs are stable: kidney function at your usual, liver tests and magnesium normal, cholesterol about where it has been. Nothing to change.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Albuterol HFA refill request. Last fill nearly a year ago, uses rarely per last note. Sent 1 inhaler, 1 refill.

reports.text:
EXAM: CT chest without contrast.
INDICATION: Surveillance, right upper lobectomy 01/2023 for stage IA adenocarcinoma.
COMPARISON: CT chest 11/10/2022.
FINDINGS: Postsurgical changes of right upper lobectomy with staple line intact and expected volume loss. No nodule or mass along the staple line. No new pulmonary nodules. No lymphadenopathy. No pleural effusion.
IMPRESSION: Expected postoperative changes. No evidence of recurrence.

documents.title: Oncology surveillance visit
documents.author: oncology
documents.body: Thoracic Oncology follow-up 07/19/2023: six months after lobectomy, asymptomatic, running again. CT 7/17 without recurrence. Next CT January 2024. NKDA.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical. 57 yo. Feeling strong, ran a 10K in July. Smoke-free over 2 years. Knees: same, occasional naproxen.
PMH: kidney tx 2018, renovascular HTN s/p transplant renal artery stent 9/2022, stage IA2 RUL adenocarcinoma s/p lobectomy 1/2023 (NED 7/2023), hyperlipidemia, COPD mild, knee OA, PUD remote.
Meds: tacrolimus 5 BID, prednisone 5, amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25, atorvastatin 40, naproxen 220 prn, albuterol prn. NKDA.
ROS negative.
Exam: vitals as charted. Skin: no suspicious lesions today, sun damage on L forearm. HEENT, neck normal. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear, healed thoracoscopy scars R. Abd soft. Joints: knee crepitus. Neuro grossly normal.
A/P: well visit. Labs per transplant mostly; CBC, A1c, UA, urine microalbumin here. Colonoscopy due 2027. Flu + updated COVID in Oct at a nurse visit. Sunscreen/sleeve on the driver's side, and to show us any sore that doesn't heal given his transplant meds.

documents.title: Transplant nephrology annual visit
documents.author: transplant nephrology
documents.body:
Transplant Nephrology
Visit: 09/13/2023

Five and a half years post-transplant. BP well controlled since last year's stent. Creatinine 1.3, tacrolimus trough in range. Recovered from lobectomy. Immunosuppression unchanged: tacrolimus 5 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily. NKDA. Return 1 year, quarterly labs.

documents.title: Nurse Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (L arm) and 2023-24 COVID (R arm). No prior reactions beyond a sore arm. Observed 15 min, fine.

orders.reason: Non-healing growing ulcer right forearm, transplant recipient

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Sore on the R forearm that won't heal. He first noticed a small rough spot around early September; it scabbed, came off, and has kept getting bigger. Not painful, bleeds a little if bumped. No fevers. Remembered our talk in August and came in.
Exam: R dorsal forearm ~2 cm ulcerated lesion with a raised rolled border and crusted center. No axillary or epitrochlear nodes. Rest of the exposed skin with sun damage only.
A/P: enlarging non-healing ulcer in a transplant recipient on tacrolimus/prednisone - high concern for skin cancer, SCC most likely. Urgent dermatology referral; derm office will see him in 3 weeks (soonest). CBC and CMP today for them.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 13.2, WBC 7.5, plt 250. Cr 1.4 (a bit above his usual 1.2-1.3), BUN 18, ALT 25, AST 30. Forwarded to transplant nephrology and dermatology. Transplant team will repeat with their next quarterly labs.

reports.text:
EXAM: Chest, PA and lateral.
INDICATION: Suspected cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma in a transplant recipient; prior right upper lobectomy.
COMPARISON: CT chest 07/17/2023.
FINDINGS: Postsurgical changes of right upper lobectomy. Lungs otherwise clear. No nodules or masses. No hilar or mediastinal enlargement. No effusion. Heart size normal. No osseous lesions.
IMPRESSION: No evidence of metastatic disease.

documents.title: Dermatology procedure visit
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Dermatology Clinic - Procedure Visit
Date: 12/04/2023

58-year-old man, kidney transplant 2018 on tacrolimus and prednisone, referred by primary care for a non-healing ulcer of the right forearm that has been enlarging over roughly three months. No fever, weight loss or night sweats.
History also notable for resected stage IA lung adenocarcinoma (1/2023).
Medications: tacrolimus 5 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, naproxen 220 mg as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: right dorsal forearm, 2.0 cm ulcer with raised, everted margins and a central keratin-filled core. No regional lymphadenopathy (epitrochlear, axillary). Full skin examination otherwise unremarkable.

Recent labs (11/13): Hgb 13.2, WBC 7,500, platelets 250,000; creatinine 1.4, BUN 18, ALT 25, AST 30.
Chest X-ray obtained today given immunosuppression and cancer history: no evidence of metastatic disease.

Procedure: after informed consent and local lidocaine, deep shave biopsy of the ulcer edge. Hemostasis with aluminum chloride. Specimen to dermatopathology.

Impression: clinically squamous cell carcinoma. Will arrange Mohs surgery once pathology confirms.
Dermatology

conditions.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of skin of right upper limb

reports.text:
SPECIMEN: Skin, right forearm, deep shave biopsy.
MICROSCOPIC: Atypical keratinocytes in nests and strands invading the dermis, with keratin pearl formation. Well differentiated. Tumor extends to the deep and peripheral margins of the biopsy.
DIAGNOSIS: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma, well differentiated.
reports.conclusion: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma, well differentiated, right forearm.

documents.title: Skin biopsy
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Derm path: invasive SCC, well differentiated, R forearm. Dermatology scheduling Mohs in January. Added to problem list. Messaged pt.
